OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and allows only secure second factors (TOTP, security keys/passkeys, GitHub Mobile; no SMS), so no account can read or change a repository's sensitive settings without MFA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: The organization's default repository permission is read (`gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission`), so a new collaborator has read access until an owner grants more by hand. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main; its only bypass actor (the maintainer) holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the review while merging a pull request and never a direct push, so a direct push to main is refused for everyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset carries a deletion rule (plus non_fast_forward) with no bypass actor, and classic protection sets allow_deletions false, so main cannot be deleted by anyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at both the organization and the repository, and GitHub Actions cannot approve pull requests; every workflow also declares permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top and elevates per job only for what that job does (id-token for publishing and attesting, attestations, security-events for CodeQL/Scorecard, contents: write only in the release job); zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run; untrusted event fields reach run: steps only through env: variables, and zizmor's template-injection audit runs in the required lint check. The review bot runs only while the organization variable CLAUDE_REVIEW_ENABLED is true and holds its secret only for same-repository pull requests.

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request trigger, which gives a fork's code no secrets and a read-only token; the one job holding a secret on a pull request (the review) runs only when the head repository is this repository, and the comment-triggered job checks out the default branch, not the pull request's code. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: Collaborator input reaches pipelines as workflow_dispatch inputs, which are passed to steps through env: rather than interpolated into scripts (zizmor's template-injection audit enforces it) and checked by the step that consumes them, e.g. pypi-install.yml waits for the index to serve exactly the version named. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/pypi-install.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D) set by a signed v* tag; release.yml's version-check job refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name (sdist, wheel, <name>-<version>.cdx.json, <tag>.attestation.jsonl), and the attestation binds each to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://bitcoin-core-rpc.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS-only; PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle, so a tampered download fails verification. https://pypi.org/project/bitcoin-core-rpc/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: Every release carries CHANGELOG.md's entry (every change) and RELEASE_NOTES.md's (what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included); the GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Build and release take dependencies through uv from PyPI with --locked against uv.lock. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA (`sha_pinning_required`); the organization's own reusable workflows are called at @main by design, and pypi-install.yml installs with pip on purpose, to test what PyPI serves.

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation, and each GitHub release since v2026.8.12 carries a Sigstore provenance bundle whose subjects are the assets' SHA-256 digests: <tag>.intoto.jsonl from v2026.10.4, <tag>.attestation.jsonl before. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and its push protection are enabled, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused; the detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run against .secrets.baseline in the required lint check for credentials GitHub does not recognise. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: The organization's policy, https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2913-L2940 : a secret is an environment secret that only the owners can reach, any other store's entry is recorded in the spending repository's REPOSITORY.md, a secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected, and the list is reviewed yearly in a "Secrets review <year>" issue. tests/secrets_test.py reads every store and refuses an unrecorded entry.

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is README.md's *Talking to a node* and *Calling* sections, docs/source/migrating.md and the API reference (docs/source/api.rst), published at https://bitcoin-core-rpc.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report issue form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for what a report needs; SECURITY.md routes a vulnerability away from the public tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md and RELEASING.md give the gh attestation verify command (with --repo and --signer-workflow, or --bundle offline) for the release assets, and RELEASING.md gives the rebuild-from-tag check that reproduces the sdist. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verification command pins the source with --repo and the signing workflow with --signer-workflow: the organization's reusable-build.yml for new releases, reusable-attest.yml from v2026.9.24 to v2026.9.29, release.yml before. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions* states that a release stops receiving security updates as soon as the next one is published, since only the latest is supported and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: Each runtime dependency's reason is written beside it in pyproject.toml; dependencies are obtained from PyPI through uv and pinned in uv.lock, and tracked by Dependabot's weekly grouped updates with a seven-day cooldown, as the standard's sections 1 and 11 state. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md names who holds access to sensitive resources: the maintainer (the only bypass actor) and the three owners, each an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments, with the command that reads them back; the tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: an issue first, one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: an issue behind it, one subject, the local gates (suite at 100% coverage, pre-commit, docs build), a Signed-off-by trailer, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/GOVERNANCE.md#L44-L46 : a grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there.

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: `lint / Sign-off` is a required status check on main (since 2026-10-03), so a pull request cannot merge unless every commit has a Signed-off-by trailer; web commits are signed off automatically (`web_commit_signoff_required`).

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/bitcoin-core-rpc/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: Nothing is compiled, so the control may not apply. Releases since v2026.9.24 attach a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM (bitcoin_core_rpc-<version>.cdx.json) covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: Classic protection on main requires the listed status checks with strict up-to-date; enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge that lands without them is a manual bypass, which is the case the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: Each release is built from this single repository; the sibling packages it depends on are released separately from their own repositories, which are held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The only non-text blobs are an empty py.typed marker and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, a Sphinx inventory (data); check-added-large-files keeps builds out of the tree.

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: The tree holds no executable or library binary. Its two non-text files are an empty py.typed marker and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, the Python documentation's Sphinx inventory, a copy of a published data file.

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') runs the test suite on every pull request and is a required status check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The documented policy is 100% line and branch coverage (standard section 8; CONTRIBUTING.md), so a change adding untested functionality fails the required test check; pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: The ruleset asks for one approving review, but the maintainer is its bypass actor and merges his own pull requests without another person's approval as everyday practice, so main does not require a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the components, their layering and every place the software reaches outside the process, and ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Trust boundaries* and *Threat model* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://bitcoin-core-rpc.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, which ruff's D rules require.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting channels and states the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L19

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org, which reaches the three organization owners. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on the repository (a CVE can be requested from them), which SECURITY.md commits to; none has been needed yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: A release's SBOM gets a vulnerabilities array with not_affected statements when a vulnerability is judged not to affect it. None is judged so today, because no Dependabot alert has been dismissed as not affecting, so the 2026.9.29 SBOM has none. The policy is in https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909 : every pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action, which fails on an added or changed dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml, and an exception is a purl named there with its reason.

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3149-L3160 : release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares before any publish job, and an advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id the release's own signed VEX document states as not affecting it.

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: Every pull request runs the Dependency review job (policy: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909), and the job is a required status check on main ("lint / Dependency review" in branch protection), so a pull request that violates the policy cannot merge.

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets the threshold at zero: ruff runs select = ALL (bandit's S rules included), and every finding is fixed or suppressed with a # noqa and a reason at its site; zizmor holds workflows to the same. CodeQL alerts have no stated threshold. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the bandit S rules, strict mypy, zizmor on workflows, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding unless suppressed in place with a reason; CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: Three organization owners (fametrano, giacomocaironi, pmazzocchi) administer every repository and are the required reviewers of the pypi and testpypi publishing environments, so any one can be absent and issues, merges and releases continue. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: None of these projects produce a user interface: each is a library, a CLI-less package or, for btclib-node, a headless full-node process with no GUI or web front end, so accessibility best practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every push to main and every pull request, and its aggregate job is a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: Pure-Python source is used directly (uv_build, no compilation step), so there is nothing whose bit-for-bit regeneration to test. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit, and sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds a release from its signed tag and verifies the rebuilt file against the release's own PyPI attestation; RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: Nearly every commit and pull request is the maintainer's; three commits are from two outside contributors. Continuity rests on the three organization owners GOVERNANCE.md names, each an administrator of this repository, not on a second maintainer. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

code_of_conduct.justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md lives in btclib-org/.github and is shown by GitHub as this repository's code of conduct through the organization's default community-health-file inheritance, confirmed via the repository's community-profile API. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule family (`select = ["ALL"]`) with a documented ignore list and runs mypy strict; CONTRIBUTING.md gives the command that enforces both, `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as required pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the gates a change must pass (suite at 100% coverage, pre-commit, docs build), the sign-off and the review; the coding standard is pyproject.toml's ruff `select = ["ALL"]` and mypy `strict = true`. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: One contributor accounts for almost all commits and pull requests (see bus_factor); no second significant contributor exists yet.

copyright_per_file.justification: Every source file (.py, .c, .h) opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: The client implements no cryptography of its own. TLS, when the RPC endpoint is https, is Python's standard library. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: The only cryptography is TLS for an https endpoint, and it is Python's ssl module; the client implements none. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: No `CERT_NONE` or unverified SSL context was found in transport.py; an `https://` request therefore verifies the server certificate by Python's own default before any data is exchanged. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_credential_agility.justification: The client reads the node's cookie file at every call, from a `cookie_path` the caller can point anywhere, so the credential lives in its own file and changes without recompilation; `rpcuser`/`rpcpassword` are the explicit alternative and are refused inside a URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_floss.justification: The only cryptography is TLS through Python's ssl module and OpenSSL, both FLOSS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_keylength.justification: TLS uses Python's default context, whose security level 2 refuses keys under 112 bits, NIST's floor for 2030. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_pfs.justification: An https endpoint uses Python's default TLS context, which since Python 3.10 disables cipher suites without forward secrecy; the floor here is 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_published.justification: The only cryptography is TLS 1.2 or later through Python's ssl module, a published and reviewed protocol. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_random.justification: generates no cryptographic key or nonce: its only random value, the JSON-RPC request id, is not a security value (and comes from secrets.token_hex anyway)

crypto_tls12.justification: Certificate verification runs through Python's `ssl` module defaults (no explicit SSLContext override was found in transport.py), and CPython's default TLS client context has required a minimum of TLS 1.2 since 3.7, which this tree's supported interpreters all postdate. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_used_network.justification: transport.py accepts both `http` and `https` URL schemes and builds requests through urllib/http.client with no explicit SSL-context override found, so an `https://` RPC endpoint gets Python's default certificate-verifying TLS; plain HTTP is what a caller chooses by using an `http://` URL, matching how Bitcoin Core's own RPC server is normally reached over loopback. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_verification_private.justification: The same default-verifying TLS handshake in transport.py completes before any HTTP request -- Basic-Auth header included -- is sent, so no private header can be sent ahead of certificate verification. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_weaknesses.justification: TLS uses Python's default context, which since Python 3.10 disables SHA-1 MAC cipher suites and requires TLS 1.2; the floor here is 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_working.justification: The only cryptography is TLS through Python's default context, which offers no broken algorithm. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

dco.justification: Since 2026-10-03 the required `lint / Sign-off` check refuses a pull request with a commit lacking a Signed-off-by trailer (the DCO), and CONTRIBUTING.md says so. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

delivery_mitm.justification: Distribution channels (GitHub, PyPI) use HTTPS exclusively.

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot's version-update and security-update ecosystems are configured in .github/dependabot.yml, dependabot_security_updates is enabled on the repository, and CodeQL and OpenSSF Scorecard run on a schedule as well. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md already carries and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, on the line the organization standard reserves for it, alongside the Scorecard badge. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the module layout and layer boundaries of this tree's software. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

documentation_current.justification: The docs build is gated in CI (docs.yml, `-W -n`) and the API reference is generated from the shipped docstrings on every release, so a documentation defect against the current release fails the gate rather than going unnoticed. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_quick_start.justification: README.md's *Talking to a node* and *Calling* sections walk a new user from install to a first RPC call. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, covers the period until 2027-09-30, is reviewed every September, and states what is intended and what is deliberately not; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* section states what the client does not protect: Basic Auth is cleartext over an http transport, credentials stay unzeroized in Python objects, a caller-supplied transport is trusted, and failed calls are not retried. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis.justification: An automated test suite with 100% statement and branch coverage runs before every release (release.yml needs the test job); mutation.yml also runs weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: The suite runs under pytest, which keeps every assert and turns every warning into an error (`filterwarnings = ["error"]` in pyproject.toml); nothing runs with python -O.

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

external_dependencies.justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model, the maintainer's bypass and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: The project site https://btclib.org/bitcoin-core-rpc/ is served over HTTPS behind Cloudflare and answers Content-Security-Policy (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security; check with curl -sI https://btclib.org/bitcoin-core-rpc/

hardening.justification: ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the flake8-bandit (S) family, so a hardening-relevant defect -- an unsafe deserialization, a weak temp-file, a shell injection -- is caught at the lint gate rather than only in review; CodeQL runs the same search at a different granularity on every push. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's secure-design argument and ARCHITECTURE.md's trust-boundary layout are the documented record of this; SECURITY.md's *Limitations* section applies it to this tree's boundary: cleartext RPC authentication, credentials held in Python objects, and a caller-supplied transport. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: The client refuses malformed input rather than passing it on: credentials inside a URL, a Decimal parameter that would need lossy rounding, and a node whose chain does not match the one asked for. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

installation_common.justification: The package is on PyPI, so `pip install bitcoin-core-rpc` (or `pip uninstall`) is the commonly-used convention for installing and removing it; README.md gives the exact command. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

installation_development_quick.justification: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command; CONTRIBUTING.md's repository-specific "The environment and the gates" section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions (site-packages, or DESTDIR-honouring behaviour inherited from pip itself); there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP (pyupgrade) and FA rule families run at `select = ["ALL"]` and flag deprecated stdlib and typing constructs; the deps-latest and deps-oldest sentinels exercise the supported interpreter range weekly, so a newly deprecated API is caught close to its deprecation. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: bitcoin-core-rpc generates no end-user text and sorts no human-readable strings; its output (RPC results, errors) is technical data. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

know_common_errors.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Common implementation weaknesses* section names the errors that matter for an HTTP client and how each is countered: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

know_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section applies the principles to this client, and an owner other than the maintainer reviewed it on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585

license_per_file.justification: Every source file (.py, .c, .h) states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/__init__.py

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported, per SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*; the upgrade path is documented instead -- RELEASING.md requires a breaking-changes check (`griffe check`) against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md carries the resulting before/after list for every source-breaking change. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

regression_tests_added50.justification: 12 of the 13 merged pull requests that close an issue and change src/ also change tests/; the suite's 100% coverage gate refuses a fix whose new code no test runs.

release_notes_vulns.justification: The v2026.10.4 release notes name every vulnerability that release fixes by its public issue (575-580, 616, 619, from the 2026-09-30 security review), with what a user does about each; none had a CVE. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/tag/v2026.10.4

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: Bugs are reported in the GitHub issue tracker with a bug-report form: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml ; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* says what belongs there.

report_tracker.justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member (organization setting two_factor_requirement_enabled = true), so nobody without 2FA can change a repository. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* section names the maintainer, the owners, repository administrators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot and Dependabot, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and has 'Only allow secure two-factor methods' selected, which refuses SMS as a second factor: only TOTP apps, security keys/passkeys and GitHub Mobile are accepted. Read from the organization's security settings on 2026-09-30 and recorded at https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: Security review of 2026-09-30 by pmazzocchi, an owner of the organization other than the maintainer: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585 . It pins its scope to a commit, checks every claim and trust boundary of ASSURANCE_CASE.md (the security requirements and boundary, https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md), states what it did not cover, and files each finding as an issue.

signed_releases.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and every GitHub release from v2026.8.12 on carries a Sigstore provenance bundle. Release tags are signed from v2026.8.12 on, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back; the latest, v2026.10.8, verifies. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/tag/v2026.10.8

sites_password_security.justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; none of these repositories runs a site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution; 8 such issues were open at some time between 2025-10-04 and 2026-10-04. The organization's standard requires one in every 12 months (README section 10). https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules, both FLOSS static-analysis tools looking for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_often.justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/actions/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification: 100% coverage floor, enforced locally and in CI: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/actions/workflows/test.yml

test_branch_coverage80.justification: Branch coverage is measured (`branch = true` in `[tool.coverage.run]`) and the 100% gate counts it: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml (search `branch = true`).

test_policy_mandated.justification: The 100% line and branch coverage floor is enforced by `fail_under = 100.0` in pyproject.toml on every pull request and stated in section 8 of the organization standard: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100.0`, gated on every pull request by the coverage job; the suite is gated well above the 80% floor this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (`fail_under = 100.0` in `[tool.coverage.report]`) on every pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml (search `fail_under`).

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the suite at `fail_under = 100.0` as a gate every change passes, so new code needs a covering test; the policy is section 8 of https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md

two_person_review.justification: The ruleset asks for one approving review, but the maintainer is its bypass actor and merges his own pull requests without another person's approval as everyday practice, so main does not require a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review [osps_qa_07_01]

updateable_reused_components.justification: Reused components are either standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped weekly by Dependabot and the deps-latest sentinel, which runs the full suite against the upgrade before it lands. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml

version_semver.justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing

version_tags_signed.justification: Every release tag from v2026.8.12 on is a signed annotated tag that GitHub verifies; earlier tags predate signing. RELEASING.md signs each tag with git tag -s and reads its signature back after the push. The tag-integrity ruleset refuses a v* tag push that brings an unsigned commit; it does not check the tag's own signature. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/tags

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: No critical vulnerability is known in the released software, which has no dependencies; the open urllib3 alerts are high and medium and reach dev tooling only.

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: The released wheel declares no dependencies. The 2026-09-30 security review findings were fixed in v2026.10.4, released 2026-10-04. No Dependabot alert is open: the urllib3 ones (dev tooling only) were fixed on 2026-10-04. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/tag/v2026.10.4

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: The findings of the 2026-09-30 security review are credited to the reviewer, pmazzocchi, in SECURITY.md's Security review section and in the review's tracking issue, https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585

vulnerability_report_response.justification: The findings of the 2026-09-30 security review are the reports of the last six months. Every code finding was fixed by 2026-10-04 (581 and 582 the same day, the rest in v2026.10.4), each with a maintainer comment. The process findings 583 and 584 have a maintainer response, with the decision due by 2026-10-14. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* section documents the private channel (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see it, and how a CVE can be requested; private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository (`gh api repos/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/private-vulnerability-reporting` answers enabled). https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: warnings are not tolerated: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are required, zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again in the lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
